title: Japan Liquidity Enhancement Auction, remaining maturities 1-5 years — the short-end reopening slot two sessions after the 20-year, and the one bucket the BoJ taper story never touches
source: EST: mof.go.jp English November 2026 auction calendar (policy/jgbs/auction/calendar/2611e.htm), fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 25,188 bytes) by the jgb-20y-auction-2026-11-18 initial research; its table row reads 'Nov. 20, 2026 | Liquidity Enhancement Auction (remaining maturities of 1-5 years)'. No size is asserted: no November row carries an announcement href on 2026-09-09 and MOF's own note on the page reads 'Each issue amount will be announced about one week prior to each auction date', putting terms around 2026-11-13. Filed `estimate` on the two counts every JGB entry on this calendar records: the size is anticipated rather than announced, and market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a non-US sovereign debt office. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: Discovered during the jgb-20y-auction-2026-11-18 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-09) on MOF's own November calendar, which lists three maturity bands for this instrument across the quarter — 1-5 years (Nov 20), 5-11 years (Nov 27) and 11-39 years (already tracked at jgb-liquidity-enhancement-11-39y-2026-10-27). It earns a slot on one term: at D+2 it is the only other JGB supply event inside this 20-year auction's plus-or-minus-five-day corridor, and its 1-5 year band sits entirely OUTSIDE both BoJ purchase buckets the super-long family has been arguing about ('more than 10 and up to 25 years', tapered, and 'more than 25 years'), which makes it the nearest thing to a same-week placebo for a demand story keyed to those buckets. Its own band is a re-opening mechanism rather than a new issue, so it carries no issue-identity question. NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED and impact is `low`: no tracked symbol carries yen-rates exposure and no house playbook is rates-keyed. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
